content: TimescaleDB (Postgres extension) gives 10-20x better time-series performance than vanilla Postgres while retaining full SQL/relational joins (useful for joining sensor readings to zones/users/devices) and native continuous aggregates + retention policies. InfluxDB is faster for pure high-cardinality write-heavy metrics but is a separate NoSQL-ish system requiring Flux/InfluxQL and extra ops overhead. For a system needing relational joins (zones, roles, devices) plus retention/aggregation, TimescaleDB is the pragmatic single-database choice; plain Postgres alone lacks native downsampling/retention/compression at scale.
